questions.prompt: A laboratory is classifying various pathogenic fungi based on their morphology in clinical specimens. An organism is identified as a monomorphic mold with hyaline septate hyphae that lacks specific structures such as arthroconidia. Which of the following fits this description?

A thermally dimorphic fungus is isolated from an HIV-positive patient in Southeast Asia. The organism is observed in tissue as small intracellular yeast-like cells that replicate by fission. Which of the following is the most likely causative agent?

A 58-year-old female with a blood glucose level of 475 mg/dL presents with eye swelling, a frontal headache, and a black necrotic eschar on her face. A biopsy of the tissue is likely to reveal which of the following morphologies
options: Hyaline, septate hyphae branching at 45-degree angles
Irregular, broad, non-septate hyphae branching at wide angles
Pseudo-hyphae with germ tube formation at 37°C

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of neutrophil dysfunction, such as chronic granulomatous disease (NADPH oxidase deficiency), is at significantly increased risk for developing a specific invasive fungal infection. Which of the following organisms is most commonly associated with this specific immune defect?

A patient being treated for invasive aspergillosis with a triazole antifungal agent reports experiencing transient visual disturbances, including seeing wavy lines and flashes of light. Which of the following medications is uniquely associated with these side effects?

A 28-year-old male presents with a pruritic, circular, erythematous rash on his forearm that has a raised border and central clearing. A KOH preparation of skin scrapings reveals hyaline septate hyphae and barrel-shaped spores. Which of the following structures is most characteristic of dermatophytes when observed in clinical specimens?

A 30-year-old veterinary worker from Bangkok develops a nodular lesion on her arm after handling an infected cat. She had received rabies post-exposure prophylaxis after a bite. Physical examination shows a solitary ulcerated nodule without lymphatic spread. A fungal infection is suspected. Which of the following laboratory characteristics best describes the causative organism?
options: Exists only as yeast at all temperatures
Exhibits thermal dimorphism, growing as mold at 25°C and yeast at 37°C
Forms nonseptate hyphae with broad branching

questions.prompt: A 24-year-old female presents with a thick, white, "cottage cheese-like" vaginal discharge and severe pruritus. Microscopic examination of the discharge shows budding yeasts and pseudohyphae. Which of the following is a recognized predisposing factor for this fungal infection?
options: Chronic use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
Poor personal hygiene in tropical climates

questions.prompt: A 45-year-old male undergoing chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukaemia develops fever and pleuritic chest pain during a period of profound neutropenia. A CT scan of the chest reveals several pulmonary nodules with surrounding ground-glass opacities. A biopsy of one of the nodules demonstrates branching, hyaline, septate hyphae that branch at 45-degree angles. Which of the following is the primary route of transmission for the pathogen responsible for this patient's condition?

A patient is prescribed an oral azole antifungal, such as ketoconazole or itraconazole. The physician explains that these drugs should not be administered along with certain classes of medications. Co-administration with which of the following classes of medications would most likely decrease the absorption and efficacy of these azoles?
